sentences.text: The name Dongbeititan combines the Chinese region Dongbei with the Greek word titan, meaning giant.
The specific name dongi honors the Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming.
Distinguishing traits include an anteroposteriorly elongated coracoid with a square end and a long, smooth, slightly convex acetabular margin on the pubic bone.
Despite its name, Dongbeititan was not exceptionally large, likely reaching lengths of about 15 meters and a weight of approximately 7 tonnes.
In 2012, an embedded tooth of the carnivorous theropod Sinocalliopteryx was found within the holotype's incomplete thoracic rib shaft.
Fossils were found in the Beipiao region of western Liaoning province, north-eastern China, within sediments of the Jehol Group.
The fossils were located in a valley between Libalang and Er Valleys, approximately 5 km northwest of the Sihetun Fossil Museum.
The holotype consists of a partial postcranial skeleton including limb bones, shoulder and pelvic girdles, and vertebrae.
Dongbeititan was a large quadrupedal herbivore like other sauropods.
Anatomical traits suggest Dongbeititan belongs to Titanosauriformes, a sauropod group within the Macronarian line.
Dongbeititan is classified within Somphospondyli but is not part of Titanosauria, which includes forms closer to Saltasaurus than to Brachiosaurus or Euhelopus.
The type species D. dongi is the first known sauropod from the Jehol Group, which is included in the well-known Yixian Formation.
Dongbeititan lived in the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of Beipiao, Liaoning, China.
Dongbeititan lived at the beginning of the Cretaceous period, between 130 and 125 million years ago during the Barremian stage in what is now Asia.
The time range for Dongbeititan is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
